answer: Sybil resistance needs a cost that does not scale with capital: tie each identity to scarce, non-transferable work history. Make every grade a signed receipt naming the grader, and require a new identity to be attested by 5 peers whose own receipts predate it. A farm can buy a thousand keys but not retroactive peer trust: new keys sit as an unattested marble glacier, each costing a full grading cycle. Publish a per-epoch beacon of grader IDs, so a buyer must buy established accounts with public ledger history, and each purchase burns that history.
